name: trusted-traveler-scheduler
what_it_holds: Python script polling the DHS Trusted Traveler Program (Global Entry/NEXUS) public appointment-availability API for open interview slots; no historical data committed; 61 stars
why_useful: Not a data source about travel volumes itself, but confirms a public, unauthenticated DHS TTP appointment API exists that a point-in-time scraper could turn into a (weak) proxy for cross-border-traveler enrollment demand/backlog over time; several near-identical sibling repos exist (mvexel/next_global_entry, arun0009/global-entry-slot-notifier, mattpopovich/GlobalEntryChecker) hitting the same endpoint.
themes: Cross-border and visa data: Schengen visa statistics, ESTA, ETIAS, CBP wait times, passport index, border crossings BTS
why_all: Not a data source about travel volumes itself, but confirms a public, unauthenticated DHS TTP appointment API exists that a point-in-time scraper could turn into a (weak) proxy for cross-border-traveler enrollment demand/backlog over time; several near-identical sibling repos exist (mvexel/next_global_entry, arun0009/global-entry-slot-notifier, mattpopovich/GlobalEntryChecker) hitting the same endpoint.

name: fuelfeed
what_it_holds: Cloudflare-Workers-based real-time UK fuel price aggregator pulling from 15+ UK retailers (ASDA, BP, Esso, Shell, Tesco, Morrisons, Sainsbury's, Jet, Gulf, Texaco, etc.) via the UK government's official Fuel Finder API/CSV feed, updated hourly to real-time, exposed as a public JSON/GeoJSON API (/api/data.json, /api/data.mapbox). mirror.mjs script performs the data mirroring.
why_useful: UK retail fuel price panel at station level, sourced from the UK govt Fuel Finder scheme -- relevant to EMEA regional driving-cost/consumer-strength proxy (a UK-specific complement to the aykutsp global country-level series), and demonstrates a clean method for turning a public government feed into a queryable API.
time_coverage: live/real-time only, no historical archive apparent
themes: Road travel and fuel: gas prices (EIA, AAA), vehicle miles travelled, holiday driving, toll data
why_all: UK retail fuel price panel at station level, sourced from the UK govt Fuel Finder scheme -- relevant to EMEA regional driving-cost/consumer-strength proxy (a UK-specific complement to the aykutsp global country-level series), and demonstrates a clean method for turning a public government feed into a queryable API.

name: global-nomad-atlas
what_it_holds: Open, community-maintained dataset (MIT, data snapshot 2026-08) scoring 80 digital-nomad cities across 40 countries (5 regions) on 12 dimensions (cost of living USD/month, internet quality, walkability, community strength, air quality, nightlife, safety, female-friendliness, LGBTQ+ acceptance, racial tolerance, English-friendliness) plus 60 coworking/coliving communities and a supplementary 16-city mainland-China dataset. Delivered as .xlsx and .csv files, PR-updatable.
why_useful: If real, a city-level nomad-friendliness/cost index (gap 16/20 adjacent) broader than Nomad List's own paywalled data.
themes: Coliving, corporate housing, furnished mid-term rental data (Blueground, Landing, Furnished Finder, Zeus), remote-work and digital-nomad data (WFH Research SWAA, Nomad List, nomad visas)
Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
wildcard: an urban economist studying platform housing effects who kno
why_all: If real, a city-level nomad-friendliness/cost index (gap 16/20 adjacent) broader than Nomad List's own paywalled data.

Directly touches Gap 16 (remote-work/long-stay demand, digital-nomad datasets) as a small but concrete, structured, city-level dataset that could proxy for long-stay/nomad demand geography relevant to Airbnb's long-term-stay segment, though it is a point-in-time snapshot (not a time series) and very new/low-traction (1 star).

A rougher, crowd-sourced cross-check on the same long-stay/remote-work theme (gap #16); city-level rather than country-level, so it could sharpen regional mix within APAC/LatAm rather than just at the country level.

name: daguar/cfpb-consumer-complaints-database
what_it_holds: Old (2013) 'meeting ground' repo — no committed data or scraper, just a discussion hub pointing users to the official CFPB Consumer Complaints database at the Socrata portal data.consumerfinance.gov and its API. 4 stars, last updated 2013, no data files.
why_useful: Confirms the canonical free source for CFPB complaints (data.consumerfinance.gov Socrata API, filterable by company='AIRBNB' and product/issue) that any of the other repos in this list, or a fresh one-off pull, would hit; low value on its own since it holds nothing.
themes: Consumer credit and BNPL: Klarna/Affirm public stats, Fed G.19, credit card delinquency, CFPB complaints dataset (Airbnb refund complaints), BBB complaint scrapers
why_all: Confirms the canonical free source for CFPB complaints (data.consumerfinance.gov Socrata API, filterable by company='AIRBNB' and product/issue) that any of the other repos in this list, or a fresh one-off pull, would hit; low value on its own since it holds nothing.

name: CFPB-Complaints
what_it_holds: SQL query file (no raw data committed) that reconstructs an 18-field, 2M+-row CFPB complaint dataset from Google's public BigQuery mirror (`bigquery-public-data.cfpb_complaints`), plus a mortgage-focused PDF report as an example of use.
why_useful: Second independent confirmation of the free BigQuery CFPB mirror and a ready SQL query to pull it; low incremental value beyond the ae-cfpb-complaint-benchmarking entry above but corroborates the access path.
time_coverage: CFPB DB inception to pull date
themes: Consumer credit and BNPL: Klarna/Affirm public stats, Fed G.19, credit card delinquency, CFPB complaints dataset (Airbnb refund complaints), BBB complaint scrapers
why_all: Second independent confirmation of the free BigQuery CFPB mirror and a ready SQL query to pull it; low incremental value beyond the ae-cfpb-complaint-benchmarking entry above but corroborates the access path.
